To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the TMDLs for PCBs in the Delaware River are exceeded by a factor of more than 10 by direct atmospheric deposition and indirect atmospheric deposition is the dominant source of PCBs in pristine watersheds.

atmospheric deposition of PCB to the tidal Delaware River is a significant source and that atmospheric deposition to the minor tributaries is the dominant source of PCBs in the minor tributary watersheds.
the atmospheric deposition of polychlorinated byphenyls (PCB) to the tidal Delaware River is a major source of PCBs, contributing about 0.7 kg sigmaPCBs year(-1), or more than 500 times the PCB TMDL.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of a mass balance model for PCBs in the Delaware River watershed and is focused on atmospheric deposition and its relationship to indirect atmospheric deposition and other sources to the Delaware River.
the atmospheric deposition and transport of PCBs to and within the Delaware River watershed and the relationship of these processes to the total PCB loading to the river.
the importance of atmospheric sources and sinks of organic contaminants in watersheds.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
atmospheric deposition of PCB to the Delaware River and its tributaries is the most important source of PCB to the river.
the atmospheric deposition is the dominant source of PCBs in the tidal Delaware River.

atmospheric deposition of PCB is a significant source of PCBs in this river, and that atmospheric deposition is a dominant source of PCBs at the watershed scale in the most pristine watersheds of the Delaware River.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the atmospheric deposition of PCB to the tidal Delaware River is the largest single contributor to the PCB loading of the river.
the TMDL for PCBs in the tidal Delaware River should include atmospheric PCB deposition as a source.
the TMDL for PCBs to the River is dominated by atmospheric deposition, but indirect atmospheric deposition is a minor component of the PCB loads to the minor tributaries.
The main takeaway from our work is that
indirect atmospheric deposition can contribute a substantial fraction of the total load of PCBs to a watershed.

atmospheric deposition is the major source of PCBs in the Delaware River and that atmospheric deposition is an important consideration for the development of the total maximum daily loads of PCBs for the tidal Delaware and its tributaries.

atmospheric deposition of PCB is a major source of PCBs for most watersheds and that the TMDL for PCB in the Delaware River will be met by reducing the direct atmospheric deposition of PCB to the river and not by reducing loads from minor tribuaries.
